address: 5901 E Lake Forest Dr, Boise (far SE 'East Columbia' bench, east of Micron / south of Gowen Rd)
owner_name: Not a single owner (Ada County withholds owner names). The 'East Columbia' developable bench is dominated by four names: J.R. Simplot Company, Micron Technology, Ball Ventures, and the Murgoitio family; the Rush Valley subdivision portion (6405 E Columbia Rd) is controlled by Conger Group and DevCo.
owner_type: Mixed — corporate agribusiness/land-bank (Simplot), semiconductor institution (Micron), Idaho investment/land-bank firm (Ball Ventures), longtime farmer-family (Murgoitio), and local developers (Conger Group, DevCo).
ownership_since: Simplot and farm families long-held (decades); Micron acquiring/annexing adjacent bench land since 2022 (ongoing through 2026). Individual parcel dates/prices not disclosed.
who_they_are: J.R. Simplot Co. = Boise agribusiness giant; Micron = Boise HQ memory-chip maker in multi-billion expansion; Ball Ventures = Idaho Falls investment/real-estate firm; Murgoitios = multigenerational Boise farming family; Conger Group (Jim Conger) and DevCo = Boise residential developers.
intent_summary: Boise FLU 'Planned Community' (+ Rural); one of three far-SE strategic planning areas the city began studying Jan 2026 ('East Columbia', east of Micron). Currently rural/farm (County RP/RUT + Boise A-1). A future planned residential community is envisioned but STALLED: owners must cooperate to fund a required secondary wildfire-evacuation road, and Simplot said it has 'no immediate plans.' Approved Rush Valley subdivision (Conger/DevCo, 420 homes on ~110 ac) is capped near 158 lots until a second access road is built.
project_status: dormant/none (area-wide planning; Rush Valley portion approved-but-capped, largely unbuilt)

address: E Columbia Rd, Boise (single ~558-ac parcel, far SE Columbia bench near the Boise River dead-end)
owner_name: Not publicly identified (Ada County does not publish owners). A single 558-ac County Rural Preservation parcel held with no active application, inside the East Columbia tract (big holdings: Simplot, Micron, Ball Ventures, Murgoitio). Consistent with an agricultural land-bank (e.g. Simplot) but NOT confirmed.
owner_type: Most likely corporate/agribusiness land-bank or a longtime farmer-family holding.
ownership_since: Long-held (agricultural, likely decades); exact date/price unknown.
who_they_are: If Simplot (unconfirmed), the J.R. Simplot Co. is Boise's dominant agribusiness and one of the two largest East Columbia landholders that told the city it has no immediate development plans.
intent_summary: Zoned County RP (Rural Preservation), Rural FLU; currently agricultural/open bench land. No active application. In the far-SE frontier where residential is blocked by the missing secondary fire road and landowner coordination. Long-term the comp plan contemplates growth; presently dormant farm/land-bank ground.

address: S Federal Way, Boise (~338 ac, Boise I-1 + County M-3/RP industrial corridor south of Gowen Rd)
owner_name: Not publicly identified. Industrial-reserve land in the airport/Gowen/Micron corridor; ownership institutional/large-holder — City of Boise (airport), Idaho Dept of Lands (state endowment), Micron, or industrial developers like Adler Industrial. Specific owner not confirmed.
who_they_are: Candidate holders: City of Boise, Idaho Dept of Lands (endowment parcels leased for industrial), Micron (annexed 358 ac at 8000 S Federal Way in 2022), Adler Industrial (city-selected to build airport-area industrial parks).
intent_summary: FLU Industrial; zoning Boise I-1 + County M-3/RP — land reserved for industrial buildout in SE Boise's principal industrial growth zone south of the airport and east of Micron. No confirmed named active project on this exact tract; reads as undeveloped industrial reserve.

address: 2472 E Warm Springs Ave, Boise (~79 ac foothills adjacent to Warm Springs Golf Course, below Table Rock)
owner_name: Mixed / mostly not publicly identified. A 44-ac portion of the hillside above Warm Springs Golf Course was donated to the City of Boise by Greg Satz and family (Council approved Oct 28 2025) for open space/trails; remaining foothills-residential parcels are privately held (owners not published).
owner_type: Private foothills landowners / potential homebuilder land-bank + City of Boise (Parks) on the donated open-space portion.
ownership_since: City acquired the 44-ac open-space piece via Satz donation Oct 2025; other parcels unknown.
who_they_are: Greg Satz and family = private foothills landowners who donated hillside acreage for preservation/trails (to Table Rock, Mesa reserve). Other owners not identified.
intent_summary: FLU 'Buildable (future growth)' / Suburban Residential, zoned A-1/A-2/R-1A — historically eyed for low-density foothills homes. Trajectory flipped to PRESERVATION: Oct 2025 Satz donation (44 ac to city open space/Ridge-to-Rivers), and Boise's Feb 2026 foothills resolution curtails new foothills development. Net: foothills-preservation frontier, not an active subdivision pipeline.
project_status: dormant/none (development curtailed; 44 ac to city open space)

address: 4747 E Warm Springs Ave, Boise (~68 ac riverside land, Barber Valley reach of the Boise River)
owner_name: City of Boise (government). Best-fit is Marianne Williams Park — a ~72-ac city riverfront park in Barber Valley donated to the City in Nov 2005 by Larry Williams honoring his late wife Marianne. Size + Public/Quasi-Public FLU align; one Suburban-Residential/R-1C parcel in the cluster may be adjacent private ground.
owner_type: Government — City of Boise Parks & Recreation (conservation/parkland), part of the 'Ribbon of Jewels' riverside parks.
ownership_since: City has owned the core parcel since the Nov 2005 Williams donation.
who_they_are: City of Boise Parks & Rec manages the site; philanthropist Larry Williams donated it to honor his wife; now a protected wetland/riparian natural area along the Boise River.
intent_summary: Public/Quasi-Public FLU; riverfront park and natural/wildlife area — conservation/open-space, NOT a development site. A smaller adjacent R-1C parcel could theoretically develop, but the controlling use is protected city parkland.
project_status: built (established public park) / not a development opportunity
